speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me diagnose this, could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis secondary to a prior distal radius fracture.
The patient's pain location, radiation to the elbow, and significant aggravation by holding an infant strongly suggest inflammation of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis tendons. While the family history of rheumatoid arthritis is concerning, the acute worsening with lifting and lack of morning stiffness make an inflammatory autoimmune process less likely than an overuse injury or post-traumatic sequela. Can you describe if you have noticed any visible swelling or deformity on the back of your wrist compared to your left hand?
